title: Pizza Margherita
subtitle: Classic Neapolitan pizza with tomato, mozzarella, and basil
excerpt: A proper margherita depends on three things: a well-risen dough, a very hot oven, and good mozzarella. This version uses bread flour for a chewy, open crumb and bakes at the highest oven temperature to get close to the heat of a wood-fired oven. The result is blistered, fragrant, and simple.
sourceNotes: Based on Neapolitan pizza-making principles. The dough hydration and high-temperature baking method follow traditional Italian technique.

content.text: Put the baking trays in the oven while it heats up so they are scorching hot before the pizza goes on. A cold tray is the main reason home pizza comes out with a soggy base.

Mix the bread flour with 7g fast-action yeast, 1 tsp salt, the olive oil, and 320ml warm water. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
While the dough rises, make the sauce. Crush the tinned tomatoes by hand. Stir in the garlic, tomato puree, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. No cooking needed.
Heat the oven to 240C. Place two baking trays inside to heat up. Divide the dough in half. Stretch each piece by hand on a floured surface into a thin round, roughly 30cm across.

Lay a pizza base on a sheet of baking paper. Spoon sauce over the base, leaving a 2cm border. Scatter over half the mozzarella. Slide onto a hot baking tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Repeat with the second pizza. Scatter fresh basil leaves over both just before serving.

items.symptom: Dough springs back and will not stretch.
items.fix: Rest it for 5 minutes, then stretch again slowly.

items.symptom: Base is soggy in the middle.
items.cause: Too much sauce or a cold tray.
items.fix: Use less sauce and make sure the tray is very hot.

items.cause: Tray not high enough in the oven.
items.fix: Move to a higher shelf for the last 3 minutes.
